I searched every `.get(` and `.header(` call in `lib/` and read the code around each match in `lib/request.js` and `lib/response.js`.

Six functions call `req.get`:

- **`lib/request.js`:**
  - `range` reads `Range`.
  - `protocol` (a getter) reads `X-Forwarded-Proto`.
  - `hostname` (a getter) reads `X-Forwarded-Host` and `Host`.
  - `xhr` (a getter) reads `X-Requested-With`.
- **`lib/response.js`:**
  - `location` calls `this.req.get('Referrer')` when the URL is `'back'`.
  - `redirect` doesn't call `req.get` itself. Its call on line 962 is `this.location(address).get('Location')`, which is `res.get`. But `res.location` calls `this.req.get('Referrer')` when the address is `'back'`. So `redirect` reaches `req.get` only indirectly, and I've included it on that basis. Drop it if you only want direct calls.

Excluded:
- `this.get(...)` inside `lib/response.js` is `res.get`.
- `res.get(...)` in `req.fresh` (`lib/request.js`, lines 478–479) is `res.get`.
- `this.app.get(...)`, `app.get(...)` and the calls in `lib/application.js` are all `app.get`.
- There are no calls to `req.header`.
